info.title: testing-rack API
info.description:
Reserve exclusive access to physical test devices. Use this website's origin as the API base URL.

1. GET /api/state to inspect available devices, max_devices, and idle_timeout_minutes.
2. POST /api/reservations with Content-Type: application/json, a unique Idempotency-Key, and {"name":"your-name","count":1}. For exact selection, replace count with "devices":["NUT001"].
3. Save the returned token privately. Execute an access_commands entry as supplied; append a quoted command such as 'uname -a' for noninteractive SSH. Standard input is streamed.
4. Resume with GET /api/reservation using Authorization: Bearer <token>.
5. When finished, DELETE /api/reservation with the same authorization header. This releases all reserved devices and terminates active gateway sessions.

Active SSH sessions refresh the idle deadline. API reads and an open browser page do not; detached work after SSH disconnects does not retain the reservation. Device availability does not establish that hardware is safe to flash or power-cycle.

get.summary: List device availability and reservation limits

post.description: No account login is required. The name is a cooperative owner identity; only one live reservation per normalized, case-insensitive name is allowed. After an uncertain response, retry with the same Idempotency-Key and body while the reservation is active. Different inputs with an active key are rejected. After release or expiry, reusing the key can create a new reservation. For HTTP 409, inspect the error code and message and refresh availability before deciding whether to retry.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique 16-128 character identifier. Reuse it only when retrying the same reservation.

201.description: Reservation created. Save token and invoke an access_commands entry. Append a quoted remote command for agent use; Standard input is streamed.

get.summary: Read the reservation authorized by a capability token
get.description: Resume with your saved token. Reading does not extend expiry. HTTP 403 means the token is invalid or expired; do not assume you still own the devices.

delete.summary: Release all devices in the authorized reservation
delete.description: Release when finished. All devices in this reservation are released and active gateway sessions are terminated. HTTP 403 means the token is invalid or expired.

bearerAuth.description: Capability token returned when the reservation is created.

token.description: Secret capability token; do not expose it.

expires_at.description: Unix timestamp. Active SSH sessions refresh the idle deadline.

access_commands.description: Complete SSH commands. Run directly for an interactive terminal or append a quoted remote command for non-TTY agent use.

actions.description: Allowed hardware actions by device name. Append a listed action to that device's access command only when your task requires it; these actions operate real hardware.
